analysis.title: Iranian attacks in the SoH could ease with mission accomplished in US midterms
key_insights: Brent fell 1.1% on 11/3 to $103.6/b after trading $100.8-107.24/b, a large reset from the Friday close of $117.64/b (Dec-26 contract). SEB attributes the drop to a risk premium for an imminent attack on Iran leaving the market after Trump stood down from threats of strikes post-midterms.
SEB says the risk of a new Trump-Israel strike is not removed and there is no proper resolution. What fell is the imminent-attack risk.

Trump said he has no immediate plans to strike Iran and noted there has been no full frontal war with Iran for about six months. SEB says the cost of full attacks became too high in April after Gulf energy infrastructure and US bases were damaged, and Iran has since regrouped and rebuilt, so the cost is now higher than at any time since April.

SEB reports Iranian officials said in October that attacks in the Strait of Hormuz (SoH) were being ramped up before the midterms to affect US gasoline and diesel prices. SEB estimates October attacks were probably twice September's level.

SEB argues Republicans losing both chambers is a strategic win for Iran that strengthens its negotiating position, and that Iran could ease SoH attacks back to September levels so more oil flows out of the Persian Gulf.
Brent Jan-27 at $103.8/b versus Oman Jan-27 at $101.3/b is read by SEB as a sign oil is flowing out of the SoH, with pressure at that point easing rather than rising.

Iran and the US are negotiating indirectly through Qatari mediators. Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaee says the US offer is unsatisfactory. Iran wants an end to the naval blockade, release of frozen funds, sanctions relief and recognition of Iran and Oman's control of the SoH, while the US wants the nuclear issue resolved.
SEB says buying of Brent Q1-27 near $100/b has probably supported the buy side somewhat after the recent high prices.

sector_views.rationale: SEB sees the imminent-attack risk premium gone from crude but the underlying risk of renewed attacks and the lack of a resolution still in place.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Down 1.1% on the day after a $100.8-107.24/b range, following the $117.64/b close on the prior Friday.
Brent had traded as high as $104.96/b by the morning of the note.
Priced above Oman Jan-27, which SEB reads as oil flowing out of the SoH.
Below Brent by about $2.5/b, which SEB reads as easing pressure at the SoH.

risk_factors: A new Trump-Israel strike on Iran cannot be ruled out and there is no proper resolution of the conflict.
Iran has regrouped, rebuilt and prepared, so the cost of a full attack for the US and its Gulf allies is higher than at any time since April.
Iran could keep or raise its attacks in the SoH if negotiations fail.
The negotiation gap remains wide on the blockade, frozen funds, sanctions and control of the SoH.
vol_and_positioning: Brent traded a wide $100.8-107.24/b range on 11/3.
SEB says buying of Brent Q1-27 near $100/b has probably supported the buy side.
geopolitical: Trump stated he has no immediate plans to strike Iran after the US midterm elections, though a Trump-Israel strike remains possible.
Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz were about twice as high in October as in September, and SEB expects them to ease toward the September level.
Republicans lost both chambers of Congress in the US midterms, which SEB says makes it harder for Trump to obtain funding for the war with Iran.

Indirect US-Iran talks run through Qatari mediators. Iran demands an end to the naval blockade, release of frozen funds, sanctions relief and recognition of Iranian and Omani control of the SoH. The US wants a resolution of the nuclear issue.
The US has maintained a naval blockade of Iran.

tension_points.bull_case: Trump stood down from immediate strikes, Iran may ease SoH attacks to September levels, and the Brent-Oman spread points to oil flowing out of the Gulf, which supports lower crude.
tension_points.bear_case: The risk of a new Trump-Israel attack remains, Iran has rebuilt, and there is no resolution of the dispute, so the risk premium could return.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A new Trump-Israel strike on Iran, or a rise in SoH attacks above September levels.

theme_stances.key_argument: The imminent risk of a Trump-Israel attack on Iran has fallen back sharply, but the risk is not removed.
theme_stances.evidence: You cannot fully remove the risk of a new attack.

theme_stances.evidence: we could see Iran easing the attacks in the SoH
